recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No current FHIR-core source edit is needed for FHIR-8054; future resource changes should continue to apply the convention when target types are narrowed or broadened.
issue_request: FHIR-8054 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification FHIR-core change request asking for consistency in why Patient references are named patient in some resources and subject in others. The resolution was to use patient when the element can reference only Patient, use subject when it can be more than Patient, and add a tool rule to enforce this convention.
initial_application: The issue was initially applied by svn revision 5822, represented in Git by commit 6f6f154d40ee7e6c03501ce974812eb7751cf8b5, which added ResourceValidator checks warning when subject was only Reference(Patient) and requiring patient to be Reference(Patient). The historical ResourceValidator.java file was later deleted during Java tooling refactoring, so the original rule text is not present in the current checkout.
additional_context: Later Jira decisions support the same convention. FHIR-19421 rejected renaming AllergyIntolerance.patient and FamilyMemberHistory.patient to subject because those elements are Patient-only; FHIR-12630 broadened Encounter from Patient-only to Patient or Group and renamed it from patient to subject. Exact FHIR-8054 Zulip and Confluence searches found no relevant conflicting community record.
reconciliation: No source change was made. A scan of all 127 active resources listed in source/fhir.ini found zero current violations: active patient elements are Reference(Patient) only, and no active subject element is only Reference(Patient). Representative checked source shows AllergyIntolerance.patient as Reference(Patient), and Encounter.subject and DetectedIssue.subject as broader-than-Patient references.

related_jiras.note: Resolved - No Change issue reaffirming that Patient-only references should remain named patient rather than subject.
Published Encounter change that renamed patient to subject while broadening the target from Patient to Patient or Group, illustrating the FHIR-8054 convention.
